checks.section.secretsAria: Confirm commits that add secret-looking values

checks.secret.desc: The files you ticked add values shaped like tokens, keys or passwords. Check them before they reach the history; the matched text is hidden here.

checks.env.undeclared: Used in code but not declared
checks.env.limit: Scan stopped at the file limit.

hygiene.name: Branch hygiene
hygiene.section.title: Branch hygiene and worktrees
hygiene.section.desc: Lists merged and stale branches, deletes merged ones after you type the name (never the current, protected or live branches), lists tags, and manages worktrees the IDE created. Worktrees made by other tools, such as Cursor, are shown read-only.
hygiene.section.enableDesc: Adds the Branch hygiene tab and its palette commands. Off: nothing is loaded.
hygiene.cmd.open: Branches: Clean up merged and stale branches
hygiene.empty.title: Nothing here
hygiene.matrix.hint: Ahead and behind are counted against each repository's default branch.
hygiene.wt.hint: Only worktrees the IDE created can be removed. Others are listed read-only and never pruned.
hygiene.wt.removeDesc: The folder is deleted; its branch stays. Git refuses when it has uncommitted changes.
hygiene.wt.newDesc: Creates a folder under the IDE's own directory and a branch intely/<name>. Type the name again to confirm.
hygiene.wt.name: Name
hygiene.wt.typeAgain: Type the name again to confirm
hygiene.wt.typeAgainAria: Type the worktree name to confirm
hygiene.del.title: Delete this branch?
hygiene.del.desc: Only the local branch is deleted, and only because it is merged. The remote is not touched; the last commit id is shown so it can be restored.

release.sinceVersion: since the commit that set {version}, {n, plural, one {# commit} other {# commits}}

remote.name: Remote
remote.device.reauth: needs a passkey check to reply
remote.chip.online: Remote · {n, plural, one {# phone} other {# phones}}
remote.chip.title: Remote is on

remote.cmd.relay: Remote: Set up my Cloudflare relay
remote.cmd.panic: Remote: Panic (revoke all devices and lock)
remote.title: IntelyIDE Remote
remote.titleDesc: Watch your agent runs on your phone, answer their questions and send follow-ups. Off by default; while off nothing runs and nothing is open.
remote.relayDesc: A Cloudflare Worker you own. It only forwards encrypted data. Only a local relay is accepted in this build.
remote.noHash: No phone app is published yet: deploy a signed build with the Cloudflare wizard below
remote.e2eNote: End-to-end encryption holds against a passive relay. The phone checks every file listed in the signed bundle, but whoever controls your Worker or your Cloudflare login could still swap the service worker itself, so protect that login.
remote.claudeRcDesc: Every Claude run started here keeps it off, so nothing can approve a tool call outside this app's rules.
remote.phonesDesc: New phones are view only. Levels, revoking and the kill switch are only available here, never from a phone.
remote.emergencyDesc: The kill switch closes every phone session and switches Remote off; devices stay paired. Panic also revokes every device and rotates the keys.
remote.auditDesc: Every pairing, answer, prompt and rejected attempt, hash-chained so a change is noticed.
remote.pair.tooLong: The link is too long for a QR code. Copy it instead.
remote.pair.scanHint: On your phone open IntelyIDE Remote (Home Screen app), tap Scan, or paste this link.
remote.pair.codeLabel: Code to read out (cannot pair alone, the phone needs the link)
remote.pair.hashLabel: Build hash to compare with the phone
remote.pair.noHash: No PWA build hash yet. Build and sign remote-web first.
remote.pair.hashWarn: The phone shows the hash of the app it is running. If they differ, do not pair: the relay may be serving a different app.
remote.pair.answered: A phone called “{name}” answered. Do the six digits on its screen match these?
remote.pair.levelNote: New phones start view only. “Can reply” lets it answer questions and allow low-risk actions; risky ones still need a passkey check, and commits, pushes and settings never work from a phone.
viewers.name: Viewers
viewers.cmd.data: Viewers: open as JSON or log tree
viewers.enableDesc: Open .json, .jsonl, .ndjson and .log files (up to 50 MB) as a searchable tree, and preview Markdown, SVG, images and PDFs, also beside the editor. Nothing is loaded until you open one.
viewers.safetyNote: Markdown never loads remote images or runs HTML, and SVG is shown as an image, so its scripts cannot run. Guarded files (secrets, .env) are not opened. PDFs open in the system viewer.
viewers.pv.nothingDesc: Open a Markdown, SVG, image or PDF file in the editor.
viewers.pv.noType: No preview for this file type
viewers.pv.noTypeDesc: Markdown, SVG, PNG, JPG, WebP and PDF files can be previewed.
viewers.pv.pdf: PDFs open in the system viewer. The IDE's content security policy keeps embedded frames to localhost, so it does not render them inline.
viewers.json.copyFailed: Could not copy to the clipboard
viewers.json.searchLines: Search lines, or a query like .[] | select(.level == "error")
viewers.json.searchKeys: Search keys and values, or a path query like .items[] | select(.status == "paid")
viewers.json.notJson: Not valid JSON, shown as text lines: {error}
viewers.json.badLines: {n, plural, one {# line looks like JSON but does not parse and is shown as text.} other {# lines look like JSON but do not parse and are shown as text.}}
viewers.json.tooLarge: Too large for the JSON viewer
viewers.json.tooLargeDesc: {size} is over the {max} cap. A JSON document has to be parsed whole, so it is not cut off. Logs and JSONL files of any size show their first 50 MB.
remote.cloud.applied: Relay switched. The new address is in use.
remote.cloud.useHint: Nothing is switched until you press this.
remote.cloud.readOnly: Read-only mode: nothing here can contact Cloudflare. Start with INTELY_CLOUD=1 to enable the relay tools only.
remote.cloud.interrupted: The last deploy did not finish. Check the Cloudflare dashboard or deploy again; it is safe to repeat.
remote.cloud.block.ack: Tick the box above to continue.
remote.cloud.group.title: Relay
remote.cloud.group.desc: The relay only forwards encrypted data between this Mac and your phone. Choose where it runs.
remote.cloud.mode.label: Relay
remote.cloud.mode.desc: Changing the mode only changes the panel below. Nothing is switched until you press “Use this relay now”.
remote.cloud.local.desc: A relay running on this Mac (loopback only). Phones outside your network cannot reach it.
remote.cloud.setup.desc: Set up your own relay on your own Cloudflare account. It runs as a Worker with Durable Objects and also serves the phone app.
remote.cloud.setup.button: Set up on my Cloudflare account
remote.cloud.frames.hint: Counted on this Mac against the Free plan's daily limit (UTC day).
remote.cloud.verdict.hashMismatch: Served build differs from the deployed one
remote.cloud.verify.blocked: The relay cannot be used while the build check is not green.
remote.cloud.manage.label: Manage
remote.cloud.manage.runbook: If the relay or a key was compromised…
remote.cloud.rotate.signingBody: A new key is prepared next to the current one. The next deploy is signed with it, and it replaces the current key only after that deploy and the relay check succeed; if they fail, the current key stays. Phones pin the old key, so every paired phone must be paired again once the key switches.
remote.cloud.rotate.vapidBody: A new push key pair is prepared next to the current one. The next deploy with push on ships it, and it replaces the current pair only after that deploy and the relay check succeed. Phones re-subscribe the next time they open the app.
remote.cloud.rollback.title: Roll back the relay
remote.cloud.rollback.body: Runs wrangler rollback on your account. The recorded phone app build may then differ from the live one; the status shows it and you can redeploy from here.
remote.cloud.forget.title: Forget this relay
remote.cloud.forget.body: Removes the profile, the signing key, the token and the push keys from this Mac. The Worker on Cloudflare keeps running; this does not touch your Cloudflare account.
remote.cloud.remove.title: Remove from Cloudflare
remote.cloud.remove.body: Deletes the Worker from your Cloudflare account. Phones paired with it must be paired again. This command will run:
remote.cloud.token.title: Replace the API token
remote.cloud.token.body: The new value replaces the stored one. This app cannot revoke the old token: delete it in the Cloudflare dashboard.
remote.cloud.logout.title: Sign out of wrangler
remote.cloud.logout.body: Runs wrangler logout on this Mac. The Worker keeps running.
remote.cloud.stopUsing.title: Stop using this relay
remote.cloud.stopUsing.body: Switches back to the relay on this Mac. The profile is kept, and the Worker keeps running on Cloudflare with its room and push subscriptions.
remote.cloud.stopUsing.wipe: Wipe the room on the relay first (revokes all paired phones)
remote.cloud.runbook.title: If the relay or a key was compromised
remote.cloud.runbook.intro: Do these in order. The first two work from this Mac, the rest are in your Cloudflare dashboard.
remote.cloud.runbook.panic: Press Panic in Settings > Remote: it revokes every phone, rotates the keys and wipes the room.
remote.cloud.runbook.rotate: Manage > Rotate signing key, then redeploy and pair your phones again.
remote.cloud.runbook.worker: In the Cloudflare dashboard delete or replace the Worker.
remote.cloud.runbook.signout: Sign out and revoke OAuth sessions in the dashboard, and sign out of wrangler here.
remote.cloud.runbook.token: Delete the API token in the dashboard and create a new scoped one if you use token mode.
remote.cloud.toast.removed: The Worker was removed from Cloudflare.
remote.cloud.unpair.title: Switching relay hosts unpairs your phones
remote.cloud.unpair.body: {n, plural, one {# phone holds} other {# phones hold}} the old address and passkeys bound to it. They must be paired again on the new relay.
remote.cloud.unpair.panic: Remote is on: the old room is wiped first, so the old relay forgets these phones.
remote.cloud.unpair.off: Remote is off: the old room, device hashes and push subscriptions stay on the old Worker until it is removed.
remote.cloud.trust.title: What you should know before using your own relay
remote.cloud.trust.e2e: Message content is end-to-end encrypted between your Mac and your phone. The relay cannot read or forge it.
remote.cloud.trust.meta: The relay sees metadata: room id, timing, sizes, IP addresses and push endpoints. Never content.
remote.cloud.trust.code: The relay also serves the phone app's JavaScript. Whoever controls the Worker or your Cloudflare login can ship hostile code to your phone, until a native app exists.
remote.cloud.trust.signed: The signed build protects against partial deploys and CDN faults. It does not protect against a stolen Cloudflare login or a hostile Worker.
remote.cloud.trust.operator: You are the operator. Use two-factor authentication on your Cloudflare account, and set a billing notification there.
remote.cloud.costs.title: Costs and limits
remote.cloud.costs.header: Numbers from Cloudflare documentation, checked {date}. They can change; the Cloudflare dashboard is the source of truth.
remote.cloud.costs.stale: These numbers are more than 180 days old. Check the Cloudflare pricing pages.
remote.cloud.costs.freeCap: On the Free plan, once a daily cap is used up the relay stays unreachable until 00:00 UTC. Nothing is charged. This Mac counts messages and warns at half of {n}.
remote.cloud.costs.unverified: Not settled in the documentation: whether the Free daily Durable Object cap counts WebSocket messages 20 to 1. In the worst case, a steady stream of 4 messages per second uses the cap in about 7 hours.
remote.cloud.costs.public: Anyone on the internet can send requests to your workers.dev address. Junk traffic counts against the caps, and on a paid plan it can cost money.
remote.cloud.costs.billing: Set a billing notification in the Cloudflare dashboard. A paid plan has no spend cap.
remote.cloud.costs.estimate: This is an estimate, not a guarantee. Wrangler does not warn you before a cap is hit.

remote.cloud.wiz.needName: Enter a valid Worker name to continue.

remote.cloud.signin.signOutAfter: Sign out of wrangler when finished
remote.cloud.signin.tokenHelp: Create a token in the Cloudflare dashboard (My Profile > API Tokens) with Workers Scripts: Edit on one account. It is stored in the Keychain and this field is cleared at once.
remote.cloud.signin.chooseAccount: Choose the account to deploy to
remote.cloud.name.label: Worker name
remote.cloud.name.rule: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, up to 63 characters.
remote.cloud.name.guessable: This name is easy to guess. The default has 12 random characters so strangers cannot find your relay by name.
remote.cloud.name.chars: Only lowercase letters a-z, digits and dashes.
remote.cloud.name.dash: No dash at the start or the end.
remote.cloud.name.pushHint: Generates push keys and sets three secrets after the deploy. Notifications never contain content.

notify.section.name: Notifications
notify.masterDesc: A banner when a run needs you, finishes or fails. Banners appear only while the IDE window is in the background; a click on one brings the run forward.
notify.soundDesc: The default notification sound with each banner.
notify.badge: Show the number of runs that need you on the Dock icon
notify.badgeDesc: Counts permission requests, questions and plan approvals that wait for an answer.
notify.body.permission: The agent is waiting for your approval.
notify.body.question: The agent has a question for you.

servers.section.name: Servers
servers.title: Servers
servers.desc: Run agents on your own machines over SSH. The agent works in the repositories on the server, with the server's CPU and its own Claude login.
servers.security: The IDE uses your SSH keys and ssh config. It never asks for a password and never accepts an unknown host key by itself: connect once from a terminal to trust a new host.
servers.empty: No servers yet. Add one to run agents on another machine.
servers.checks: What is installed on the server
servers.loginNotice: Claude is not signed in on this server, or this could not be checked. Sign in once on the server:
servers.deleteBody: The server is removed from the IDE. Nothing is deleted on the server itself. A server with live runs cannot be deleted.
servers.copy.failed: Could not copy the SSH command
servers.repos.title: Repositories on {name}
servers.repos.cloneNote: Cloning runs on the server with the server's own git credentials.
servers.repos.cloneFailed: {count, plural, one {# repository could not be cloned} other {# repositories could not be cloned}}
servers.setup.title: Set up {name}
servers.setup.node: Node 24 (only when the server has no Node 24 or newer)
